replication.target_description: Study 1 replication using dichotomized original numeracy scale: interaction of numeracy group with positive-negative framing on student-performance ratings, mixed ANOVA; main report p. 11 and Table 9 p. 12.

n.location: Published report p. 7, Participants; p. 11, Results introductory paragraph.
n.quote: we had 860 participants ... In this section, we reported the results of the sample ... without exclusion. ... Therefore, we focus our analyses on the full sam- ... ple.
n.sample_role: Participants in the shared full sample used for the four replication studies and primary analyses without further exclusions.
n.exclusions: 919 recruited; 59 failed initial verifications or consent and were filtered out, leaving 860. Main results explicitly use the full sample without subsequent preregistered exclusions; post-exclusion results are separately supplementary.

es.location: Published report p. 11, Replication: Dichotomized numeracy, Study 1 paragraph; corroborated Table 9 p. 12.
es.quote: interaction effect of numeracy on framing effect (F(1, 855) = ... 5.02, p = .025, η2p = 0.01, 90% CI [0.00, 0.02])

reported_success.location: Published report p. 11, Replication: Dichotomized numeracy, Study 1 paragraph.
reported_success.quote: We concluded support for the hypothesis ... that the less numerate show a stronger framing effect than ... the highly numerate, with weaker effects.

notes: Identity assessed from supplied canonical text: title and authors Minrui Zhu and Gilad Feldman match the neutral replication reference; the document is the published Stage 2 Replication Registered Report in Collabra: Psychology 9(1), 2023, DOI 10.1525/collabra.77608, and explicitly identifies materials/data/code at https://osf.io/4hjck/. Thus this is the published version of the named 2022 OSF project, with results and appended supplementary material, rather than a preregistration or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Target located by Study 1, framing outcome, dichotomized numeracy, requested partial eta-squared, and p. 11 locator, independently of row order or numerical matching. N=860 is based on the explicit final participant count and the Results statement that these analyses use the full sample, not on df or a sum. Supplement Table S18 prints F(1, 855) = 4.42 with p = .025, whereas the target main paragraph and Table 9 print F(1, 855) = 5.02 with p = .025; retained the main-report statistic and printed effect size without correction. Same-test p = .025 is recorded here as context only because p_r is unassigned; its core field remains a placeholder. Original side is unassigned. The authors call the target hypothesis supported with weaker effects; successful codes this Study 1 verdict, not their mostly-successful project-wide verdict.
